meta.subtitle: Shares have halved from their high; cheap on adjusted earnings, but leverage and Middle East disruption are real risks

analystSentiment.commentary:
ESAB's share price has fallen hard. At $69.90 on October 2, 2026 the stock sits near its 52-week low of $64.83 and about half its high of $137.42. The data we hold does not say what drove the decline, and we have no news coverage that explains it; that gap is the main uncertainty in this report.

The filing shows two plausible pressures: higher leverage after the Eddyfi acquisition (see Financials) and disruption from the Middle East conflict (see Risks).

Against that, revenue is still growing, the Street remains positive, and the shares now trade at a low multiple of consensus earnings (see Valuation). We think the price discounts more damage than the filing shows, but we keep our target well below the Street's.

We rate ESAB BUY with a $75–$95 target range.

executiveSummary.companyOverview:
ESAB Corporation formulates, develops, manufactures and supplies consumable products and equipment for cutting, joining and automated welding, as well as gas control equipment. It sells through independent distributors and direct salespeople to a highly diversified industrial customer base.

The company describes itself as a focused premier industrial compounder, run under its ESAB Business Excellence system, EBXai. On June 1, 2026 it acquired Eddyfi, headquartered in Québec, Canada, for consideration transferred of approximately $1.5 billion.

ESAB was founded in 1904 and is headquartered in North Bethesda, Maryland. The 10-K says approximately 80% of its 2025 sales came from operations outside the United States.

thesis.label: BUY
thesis.body: The market is pricing ESAB as if its earnings power were impaired. The filing shows a business whose revenue is still growing, with consensus expecting higher earnings in FY26E and FY27E. If ESAB delivers anything close to consensus and starts reducing leverage, the shares should recover part of the decline. Our target sits well below the Street's to reflect the balance sheet.

catalysts: Integration of Eddyfi and its contribution to results.
Easing of Middle East logistics disruption.
Any recovery of IEEPA tariff refunds, which ESAB has not yet recorded as receivables.
risks: High leverage after the Eddyfi acquisition.
Continued Middle East and Ukraine-related disruption.
A cyclical downturn in industrial capital spending.
A share-price decline our data does not explain.

income.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.incomeCommentary:
FY25 revenue was $2.8B, up {+3.7%+}, after a {-1.2%-} dip in FY24. Operating margin peaked at 16.3% in FY24 and eased to 14.5% in FY25; diluted EPS was $3.67, down from $4.31.

In the quarter ended July 3, 2026, which our data labels Q3'26, revenue was $807.6M, up 12.9%; that period includes Eddyfi from June 1. Operating margin for the quarter fell to 9.7%, and the trailing net margin is 5.7%. The MD&A attributes part of the pressure to geopolitical disruption and tariffs (see Risks). The excerpt does not break out acquisition-related costs, so we cannot say how much of the margin decline is one-off.

This is the counter-case to our BUY: margins are falling at the same time as leverage has risen.

balance.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.balanceCommentary:
Total debt was $1.2B and net debt $1B at the end of FY25, before the Eddyfi acquisition. Trailing net debt to EBITDA is 4.7x, a high level for a cyclical industrial, and the trailing current ratio is 1.96. The excerpt does not say how Eddyfi was financed.

Separately, in February 2026 ESAB placed 6.50% Series A Mandatory Convertible Preferred Stock with an aggregate liquidation preference of $175.0 million. That preferred ranks ahead of common equity and will convert into common stock, so holders face future dilution as well as higher leverage.

cashflow.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.cashflowCommentary:
Free cash flow was $213.3M in FY25, a 7.5% FCF margin, down from 11.1% in FY24. Capital expenditure was small relative to revenue. The proxy reports free cash flow of $246.1 million for FY25 on the company's own definition; we use the figure from our data, which is lower.

At FY25 levels, free cash flow would reduce leverage only slowly, so deleveraging depends on margins recovering and on Eddyfi's contribution. The dividend is small relative to cash flow and does not constrain the balance sheet.

multiples.note: Peer multiples pending a peer data source.

valuation.multiplesCommentary:
At $69.90 ESAB trades at 25.3x trailing earnings, 12.8x NTM earnings, ~10.8x FY27E earnings, 1.4x trailing sales and 14.1x trailing EV/EBITDA.

The gap between trailing and forward multiples is large. Consensus EPS is $5.45 for FY26E and $6.48 for FY27E, well above FY25 diluted EPS. The proxy reports FY25 core adjusted earnings per share of $5.27, so consensus is most likely on that adjusted basis; on GAAP earnings the shares are more expensive than the forward multiple suggests.

The Street is strongly positive: 10 Buy and 1 Hold, with a consensus target of $126.91, a median of $128.00 and a range of $100.00–$145.00. Even the lowest Street target is well above today's price.

We have no peer multiples to compare against.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: Eddyfi integrates smoothly, Middle East disruption eases, margins recover and debt falls. The market regains confidence and the shares move into the Street target range.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: ESAB delivers close to consensus adjusted earnings, begins reducing leverage, and the forward multiple recovers part of its decline. The shares settle roughly halfway between today's price and the lowest Street target of $100.00.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: Industrial demand weakens while leverage is high, estimates fall, and the market continues to price ESAB as a stretched, cyclical balance sheet. The shares break below the 52-week low.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
Base carries the most weight because it needs only partial delivery against consensus and a partial recovery in the multiple. Bear carries more weight than Bull because leverage is high and margins fell in the latest quarter. Bull still carries a quarter of the weight because the Street's targets show how far sentiment could recover if execution holds.

The result is a weighted fair value of $80.75, an expected upside of +15.5% and a bear-case downside of -28.5%. The reward/risk clears our BUY threshold, but only modestly, which is why we do not go further.

Our $75–$95 target range brackets Base.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: Our data carries ESAB as one consolidated segment, while the 10-Q MD&A says the company reports two: the Americas, covering North and South America, and EMEA & APAC, covering Europe, the Middle East, India, Africa and Asia Pacific. Because our data carries no segment figures, we present the consolidated total and quote no split. The geographic breadth gives ESAB exposure to Europe and emerging markets as well as North America.

moatFactors.name: Consumables and equipment mix
moatFactors.body: The MD&A describes a business mix balanced between equipment and consumables, and between high-growth and developed markets, which management believes helps mitigate cyclical exposure. In our view, consumables give ESAB a steadier revenue stream than equipment alone would.

moatFactors.name: Brand and distribution
moatFactors.body: ESAB has operated since 1904 and sells through independent distributors and direct salespeople worldwide, with principal manufacturing facilities in 16 countries outside the United States. That scale and reach are hard for a small entrant to match.

moatFactors.name: Business system and acquisitions
moatFactors.body: Management says its experience of acquiring and integrating businesses positions it to capture future opportunities, and EBXai is meant to drive continuous improvement. The Eddyfi acquisition is the current test of that claim.

businessMoat.durability: We rate the moat NARROW. An established brand, broad distribution and a balanced product mix protect the core business. Operating margin has moved between 12.6% and 16.3% over FY21 to FY25 and fell to 9.7% in the latest quarter, so the moat has not protected margins from the current pressures. The 10-K says the welding and cutting industry is mature and cyclical in developed markets, which limits pricing power.

points: Consensus expects FY26E revenue of ~$3.1B, up 8%, and FY27E revenue of $3.4B.
Eddyfi's revenues totaled approximately $240 million for 2025, per the MD&A, and the business moves ESAB into advanced inspection and monitoring technologies.
Management expects strategic acquisitions to contribute to growth; in our view, the capital-allocation constraints set out in Management make further large deals unlikely in the near term.
The MD&A says ESAB has received an insignificant amount of IEEPA tariff refunds so far and has recorded no refund receivables. Any further refunds would be upside not in the current numbers.

management.leadership: Per the proxy statement dated March 2026, Shyam P. Kambeyanda is President and Chief Executive Officer and Kevin J. Johnson is Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer. The proxy says management recommended that executive officers forgo their cash bonuses for fiscal 2025, given results against expectations, and the Board accepted. That is a sign of accountability. These facts predate the 10-Q and may have changed.
management.capitalAllocation:
The Eddyfi acquisition is the defining capital-allocation decision of 2026. Paying approximately $1.5 billion for a business with 2025 revenues of approximately $240 million is a high price, and its success depends on growth and synergies that the filing does not quantify.

ESAB pays a small dividend; our data shows no repurchase amounts for FY21 to FY25. In our view, cash flow should go to reducing leverage, and we would view a new large acquisition in the near term as a negative.
management.governance:
Per the proxy statement dated March 2026, the Board determined that Mr. Rales, Mr. Allender, Ms. Cummings, Ms. Jordan, Mr. Lutz, Dr. Martin, Ms. Phillipps, Mr. Teirlinck and Mr. Vinnakota are independent. Mitchell P. Rales is the independent Chairman and a significant stockholder; the excerpt does not give his ownership percentage. The Board held 11 meetings during 2025.

The proxy discloses two related-person transactions involving Mr. Rales: a stadium suite rented from a team whose ownership group includes him, for a $303,187.50 license fee for the 2025 - 2026 season, and his agreement to purchase $100.0 million of the Mandatory Convertible Preferred Stock. On the preferred, he recused himself from the Board's discussion and abstained from its vote, and an independent pricing committee approved the terms.

For common holders, this cuts both ways. A Chairman with a large economic stake has strong reasons to restore value, but through the preferred he now also holds a claim that ranks ahead of theirs. The recusal and independent pricing are appropriate safeguards; we would watch for further transactions of this kind.

idiosyncratic: Integration: the Eddyfi purchase is large relative to ESAB's existing business. If integration or synergies disappoint, the balance sheet set out in Financials leaves little room for error.

Geopolitical disruption: the MD&A says the Middle East conflict, including logistics challenges from the closing of the Strait of Hormuz, decreased sales levels and increased inventory costs during the six months ended July 3, 2026. The war in Ukraine adds further uncertainty.
Asbestos and legacy liabilities: the filing lists asbestos-related liabilities, insurance coverage litigation and the solvency of insurers among its risks, alongside pension obligations.
Information gap: the share price has fallen further than the filing alone explains to us, which may reflect news or estimate changes we do not hold.
risks.systemic: The 10-K says demand for welding and cutting products depends largely on capital spending in manufacturing and industrial sectors, and that the industry has contracted during periods of slowing industrial activity. Tariffs on steel and aluminum and retaliatory trade measures add cost and demand risk; the MD&A says the IEEPA tariffs remain subject to ongoing litigation. With most sales outside the United States (see Overview), currency movements also matter.

body: BUY, target range $75–$95, based on the scenarios in Valuation.
We would add conviction on evidence of reduced leverage and margin recovery in the next two quarters. We would cut to HOLD if consensus estimates start falling or if Eddyfi integration slips.
